conventions.head: fixed; eyes rotate about their own centres
conventions.eye_object: camera named EYE: local -Z primary gaze, local +Y head up
conventions.equirect_pixel_to_eye_direction: lon=(u-0.5)*2pi, lat=(0.5-v)*pi, v=0 top; d=(sin lon cos lat, sin lat, -cos lon cos lat)
conventions.depth_pass: ray distance from the eye centre (Blender 5.2, equirect camera)

measured_with.note: first run of this pipeline on a GPU; the handover was verified on CPU only

scenes.notes: Closed room, so zero holes and zero back-faces as expected. Nadir and zenith both 1.600 m confirm metric scale (eye 1.6 m, floor 0, ceiling 3.2 m). Contact sheet matches the CPU reference in reference/calib_room_sheet.png structurally, so the OptiX path reproduces the sandbox result. 50 targets in calib_room.targets.json.

Column shift exactly 0: the render reproduces the source mapping. Negative control confirmed on this machine - a 90 deg mis-rotated eye is reported as 512 px = W/4. hole_fraction is 1.0 by construction (environment at infinity). The 1.5% median error is NOT a mapping error: it is the mismatch between Cycles' default Blackman-Harris reconstruction filter and the exact 4x4 box average inspect_preview.py compares against. Re-rendering with pixel_filter_type=BOX, filter_width=1.0 drops it to 0.0032 (p99 0.047); raising samples 16 -> 512 changes nothing (0.01517 -> 0.01540), which is what rules out sampling noise. Use a box filter for the tier-1 identity check.

Scene '_mainScene' (Cycles, metric, unit scale 1.0); the file also holds dustParticules and volumeLight, both EEVEE, neither used. EYE placed headlessly with tools/place_eye.py and saved beside the original, which stays pristine. nadir 1.200 m equals the chosen eye height exactly, so metric scale is confirmed; zenith puts the ceiling at 2.90 m. Remaining 2.1% holes are the window panes only, escaping to a featureless world background - usable, but a real environment behind the windows would be better for gaze directions that cross them. First look from the file's own shot camera (previews/classroom_shotcam) failed badly: renderCam sits 0.46 m off the rear wall (depth_min 0.10 m) and sees its back side, giving backface_fraction 0.136. Moving the eye into the room cut that to 0.0038, a 36x reduction - the README's 'set dressing built for one shot camera' warning, measured.
